paragraphs: Rain adapts military and civil autonomous aircraft to perceive, understand, and suppress wildfires. The company says the technology equips fire agencies with a new layer of safety for human-piloted missions and supports command of a network of uncrewed aircraft prepositioned in remote areas. Its wildfire mission autonomy system perceives the fire, reads its behavior, size and direction of spread, and uses that information to design a suppression strategy.

Rain and Sikorsky, a Lockheed Martin company, have demonstrated autonomous wildfire suppression technology in a representative wildfire environment in California. That work included communication interoperability of an autonomous aircraft with a human-piloted helicopter in the same Fire Traffic Area, supervised by an Orange County Fire Authority air tactical group supervisor aircraft. The two companies also said they would explore how Sikorsky's MATRIX autonomy suite operating with Rain's Wildfire Mission Autonomy System can launch uncrewed helicopters to drop water on wildfires within minutes of detection.

Rain announced a partnership with Brothers Air Support, a private Black Hawk firefighting operator, to equip their helicopter with Rain's wildfire perception system. The work goes back to 2019, when Bryan, Ephraim and Max started building the MK1 prototype. That prototype produced a fully autonomous demonstration of a drone system detecting and suppressing a wildfire ignition in approximately 40 acres of forest.

quote.text: Rain’s wildfire intelligence system builds a strategy that considers subsequent responding aircraft, incorporating their resources and arrival times into an optimal suppression strategy.
